_comment: Named environments for /wowlidate. A target names WHERE a catalog runs — never how hard. Lanes, policy and repair stay a per-run decision. No credential ever belongs in this file: it is tracked in git. Secrets live in .env, and a target only names the keys that must be set.

humi-sit.description: HUMI SIT, with the humi-SIT repo index and the HRCenter-SIT database behind it.

db._comment: Coordinates only. The password lives in .env (WOWLIDATOR_DB_URL) and never here — this file is tracked in git.
db.source: k8s-config /sit/config/benefit-management/.env — Azure DevOps centralgroup/'Product - Humi', needs a PAT with Code (Read)
db.note: not localhost. The app-facing string names 10.179.72.9 and is reachable only over the FortiClient VPN; a WOWLIDATOR_DB_URL pointing at localhost silently proves nothing and cost a run on 2026-09-07.

reach.note: needs FortiClient VPN — without it the host is NXDOMAIN, which has killed a relaunch on its own

requires.WOWLIDATOR_AS: the fallback account, used for the first persona a row names
requires.WOWLIDATOR_DB_URL: HRCenter-SIT — must match the db block below: 10.179.72.9:5432, search_path benefit_management,public

optional.WOWLIDATOR_DB_REMOTE_OK: 1 — this database is remote, and the client refuses a remote write without it
optional.WOWLIDATOR_DB_RESTORE_URL: unset here, so `wowlidator db restore` cannot put the tables back after a mutating run

notes: The repo index carries the schema: 14 tables, alongside 336 routes, 136 API operations and 872 components. A run without --repo degrades claims that assert database state to what the UI alone shows.
Every configured persona points at the same account, so role-separation cases do not really prove role separation. Say so in a report rather than passing quietly.
The indexed schema is benefit_management alone (14 tables), not all 489 in HRCenter-SIT. A claim needing employee or workflow tables cannot see them — widen the dump rather than wonder why.
